title: Growth Marketing Automation Zapier Alternative: 2026 Guide
summary: Growth marketing automation Zapier alternatives vary by cost and maintenance needs. Find which fits your budget and your team's technical skills.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces (Open-Source Option)


For teams that want a no-code builder with branching that a non-coder can edit, Activepieces offers an MIT-licensed core, and its 750 integrations can be counted in the community integrations folder of its public GitHub repository, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, meaning the integration ecosystem reflects what users actually need.


You can run it on your own server, in exchange for a smaller app catalog than Zapier's.


It has a free and paid cloud plan, and the code can be self-hosted.


On the cloud plans the meter is the run: Activepieces' published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, set against the per-task billing on Zapier's pricing page and the per-module billing on Make's.


A ten-step lead flow therefore costs the same as the two-step workaround it replaced, and splitting work into smaller steps carries no penalty. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


On self-hosting, the cost is clearer. An n8n Community cost breakdown puts Activepieces at $95.99 per month at the top end, against $800 per month for n8n.


At that scale, the same heavy workload costs about one-eighth as much, so the gap matters most for high-volume campaigns.


You pay for something different when you self-host: servers and someone's time instead of a charge per run, so a campaign that fires thousands of times costs no more in software fees.


Branching is part of the builder, so routing by lead source or score doesn't force you onto a higher plan. A lead-form flow looks like this:


1. Set the trigger to a new lead form submission.
2. Add a filter step that stops the run when the email is blank or from a throwaway domain.
3. Add a CRM step that creates the contact, or updates it if the email already exists.
4. Post the lead's name, source and message to a Slack channel for your sales team.
5. Run a test with a real submission, check the CRM record and the Slack post, then publish.


Without step 2, junk leads reach the CRM, and without step 3 you get duplicate contacts.


The catalog is smaller than Zapier's, so check each marketing app you rely on against Activepieces' current integrations list before you commit. The free plan allows 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows; I haven't confirmed the paid plans' list prices here.


It suits teams with a technical maintainer, branching-heavy workflows, and a need to keep data on their own server. It's a poor fit if your stack depends on niche apps that you can't confirm it connects to.


Activepieces is the better choice for teams whose automations run to many steps and who judge a tool by how predictably its bill tracks usage.


Its pricing page charges **1 credit per flow run, however many steps** the flow contains, whereas Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so adding branches or splitting work into smaller steps never raises the cost.


Zapier's larger app catalog may suit teams that need a specific integration, but for the criterion this article leads on, where the run is the meter, Activepieces' billing unit is the simpler one to plan around.
